name: Vernal-Spandrel
description: Rolling continents break around shallow seas, their interiors scored by massive canyon systems. Beyond towering mountain ranges, the land runs to a horizon that feels hand-drawn.

Storm season reorganizes all plans. When the pressure falls, animals go quiet, instruments drift, and the horizon turns the color of an old wound. Forests of black-leaved flora drink the dim light and exhale a scent like cold iron.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.

For traders, biomass, platinum, iron and solar potential alone justifies the crossing; for everyone else, the planet pays in questions. Fuel is cheap, information is not, and both are dangerous to carry.
